questions.question_text: Function f: R → R, f(x) = x³ is:
questions.explanation: The function f(x) = x³ is one-to-one because each output value corresponds to exactly one input value (if x₁³ = x₂³, then x₁ = x₂), and it is onto because every real number is a cube of some real number, so the range equals the codomain R.

The inverse sine function sin⁻¹(x) is only defined when its input x lies within the range of the sine function. Since sine outputs values between -1 and 1 for all real angles, the domain of sin⁻¹(x) is [-1, 1].

When you multiply a matrix by its transpose, the result is always symmetric because (A·A^T)^T = A·(A^T)^T = A·A^T, which equals itself. This property holds for any matrix regardless of its dimensions.

For an upper triangular matrix, the determinant equals the product of its diagonal entries. This can be verified by expanding along the first column repeatedly—each step eliminates a row and column, eventually leaving only diagonal elements to multiply.

questions.question_text: Order of differential equation y' + y² = 0:
questions.explanation: The order of a differential equation is determined by the highest derivative present. In y' + y² = 0, the highest (and only) derivative is y', which is the first derivative, making this a first-order differential equation.
This is a separable differential equation. Separating variables gives dy/(1+y²) = dx/(1+x²). Integrating both sides yields tan⁻¹(y) = tan⁻¹(x) + C, since the integral of 1/(1+u²) is tan⁻¹(u).
Using the chain rule: the derivative of e^(sin x) is e^(sin x) times the derivative of the exponent (sin x). Since d/dx(sin x) = cos x, the result is cos x · e^(sin x).
Using the chain rule: d/dx(ln(cos x)) = (1/cos x) · d/dx(cos x) = (1/cos x) · (-sin x) = -sin x/cos x = -tan x.

questions.question_text: Area of region bounded by y = √x and y = x:
questions.explanation: The curves intersect where √x = x, giving x = 0 and x = 1. Since √x > x on (0,1), the area is ∫₀¹(√x - x)dx = [⅔x^(3/2) - ½x²]₀¹ = ⅔ - ½ = 1/6.
The cross product i × j follows the right-hand rule in the standard Cartesian coordinate system. Point your fingers in direction i, curl them toward j, and your thumb points in the direction of k.
The dot product of (1,0,0) and (0,1,0) equals zero, which means the vectors are perpendicular. The angle between perpendicular vectors is always 90°.

questions.question_text: Equation of plane through origin with normal (a,b,c):
questions.explanation: A plane with normal vector (a,b,c) has equation a(x-x₀) + b(y-y₀) + c(z-z₀) = 0. Since the plane passes through the origin (0,0,0), this simplifies to ax + by + cz = 0.

questions.question_text: Distance from (0,0,0) to plane x + y + z = 6:
questions.explanation: The distance from a point to a plane ax + by + cz = d is |ax₀ + by₀ + cz₀ - d|/√(a² + b² + c²). Substituting (0,0,0) into x + y + z = 6 gives |0 - 6|/√(1 + 1 + 1) = 6/√3 = 2√3.
Bayes' theorem states that P(A|B) · P(B) = P(A∩B), which is the definition of conditional probability. By symmetry, P(B|A) · P(A) also equals P(A∩B), so both expressions are equivalent.

questions.question_text: Mean of Poisson distribution with parameter λ:
questions.explanation: For a Poisson distribution, the mean equals the parameter λ. This is a fundamental property of the Poisson distribution where both the mean and variance equal λ.
The variance of a binomial distribution is np(1-p), and standard deviation is the square root of variance. Therefore, the standard deviation of B(n,p) is √(np(1-p)).

questions.question_text: Solution of linear programming has optimum at:
questions.explanation: The optimal solution of a linear programming problem occurs at a vertex (corner point) of the feasible region because the objective function is linear, and linear functions achieve their maximum or minimum values at the extreme points of convex polygonal regions, not in the interior or arbitrary locations.

questions.question_text: Convex polygon has interior angles summing to:
questions.explanation: For any convex polygon with n sides, the sum of interior angles equals (n-2)·180°. This formula derives from dividing the polygon into (n-2) triangles from a single vertex, and since each triangle has angles summing to 180°, the total is (n-2)·180°.

questions.question_text: Eccentricity of x²/4 + y²/9 = 1 (b > a means vertical major):
questions.explanation: For an ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 with b > a, the major axis is vertical. Here a² = 4 and b² = 9, so a = 2, b = 3. Eccentricity is e = √(b² - a²)/b = √(9 - 4)/3 = √5/3.
The given line 3x + 4y = 5 has slope -3/4 (from rearranging to y = -3/4 x + 5/4). Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals, so the perpendicular slope is -1 ÷ (-3/4) = 4/3.

questions.question_text: If z₁ = 1 + i and z₂ = 1 - i, z₁ · z₂ = ?
questions.explanation: Multiply using FOIL: (1 + i)(1 - i) = 1 - i + i - i² = 1 - (-1) = 2. This is the difference of squares pattern (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b².

questions.question_text: Number of ways to choose 3 from 7:
questions.explanation: Using the combination formula C(n,k) = n!/(k!(n-k)!), we get C(7,3) = 7!/(3!4!) = (7×6×5)/(3×2×1) = 210/6 = 35.
